extra.message: Password reset token disclosed in API response enables account takeover — Full account takeover of any user (including property_admin) by anyone who knows the victim's email address, with no access to their inbox or any other credential required. [verified: request_password_reset returns the raw reset token in the JSON response body to any unauthenticated caller who supplies a valid email, and confirm_password_reset (line 130+) accepts that token to set a new password, giving full account takeover with no email access needed.]

SSRF via internal relay endpoint — Server-side requests to internal services or cloud metadata endpoints (e.g. 169.254.169.254), enabling internal network reconnaissance and credential theft [verified: _wrk_gate only compares a header to a static env token via non-constant-time '!=' with no session/role/tenant check, and url is passed unsanitized to urlopen enabling SSRF to internal/metadata endpoints.]
SSRF via secondary relay endpoint — Internal network/cloud-metadata access via server-side fetch [verified: Same weak gate; endpoint param flows unsanitized into urlopen, a second SSRF sink.]

Server-side template injection — Remote code execution via Jinja2 sandbox escape / arbitrary Python object access [verified: fragment is concatenated directly into Jinja2 Template source and rendered, enabling full SSTI/RCE via template syntax.]

Path traversal arbitrary file write — Overwrite or plant arbitrary files anywhere the process can write, potentially leading to RCE via web-accessible paths or config overwrite [verified: name is joined into BASE_EXPORT_DIR with no sanitization and raw request body is written to that path, allowing arbitrary file write.]

OS command injection via ping endpoint — Full remote code execution as the application's OS user [verified: host is string-concatenated into a shell command passed to os.system with no quoting/allowlisting, enabling shell metacharacter injection.]

IDOR on tenant ID documents across buildings — Any property manager or maintenance worker, regardless of building assignment, can download any tenant's uploaded ID document via GET /documents/{id}/download, exposing PII portfolio-wide [verified: authz.py:135 grants any non-tenant role (property manager, maintenance worker) unrestricted access to tenant-ID documents with no building/assignment scoping check, unlike sibling branches which call can_access_building/manager_building_ids.]

Path traversal arbitrary file read — Read arbitrary files on the server filesystem (e.g. ../../etc/passwd, application secrets, .env) [verified: packet_ref is concatenated into BASE_EXPORT_DIR with no traversal sanitization and read_text() returns file contents to the caller.]

Path traversal file write plus plaintext PII storage — Arbitrary file write outside intended directory and persistence of sensitive PII (SSN, card number) in plaintext [verified: ref is interpolated unsanitized into a file path and plaintext SSN/card data is persisted to disk, combining path traversal write and plaintext PII storage.]

NoSQL injection via mongo lane endpoint — Bypass query logic, extract arbitrary documents, or trigger DoS via crafted operators [verified: Attacker-supplied JSON is passed directly as the MongoDB filter to find_one with no schema validation, enabling operator injection.]

XML external entity injection (XXE) — Server-side file disclosure and SSRF via crafted DOCTYPE/ENTITY declarations [verified: XMLParser is explicitly configured with load_dtd=True and resolve_entities=True over attacker-supplied XML body, enabling XXE.]

Webhook URL SSRF via missing address validation — Admin-supplied webhook URLs pointing at internal services/cloud metadata are accepted without restriction, enabling SSRF once/if delivery consumes the URL [verified: WebhookIn.url only enforces an http(s):// prefix regex with no denylist for loopback/link-local/metadata addresses (127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254, etc.), so a malicious or compromised admin can register such URLs unimpeded; severity is capped at medium since no outbound dispatch code currently consumes WebhookEndpoint.url and the endpoint is restricted to ROLE_PROPERTY_ADMIN.]

Session cookie missing Secure flag — Session token interception via network MITM/protocol downgrade, leading to account takeover [verified: security.py:66 hardcodes secure=False with no environment conditional, so the httponly session cookie is sent over plaintext HTTP allowing token interception via network MITM.]

Mass assignment of privileged fields — Attacker can set arbitrary fields including role/approved/balance, illustrating a broader unrestrained-update pattern usable for privilege escalation [verified: workset.update(payload) merges arbitrary attacker JSON into a privileged dict with no field allowlist, letting attacker set role/approved/balance.]

CSV formula injection in report exports — A low-privileged tenant can plant a formula in their profile/ticket data that executes when staff open the exported CSV in Excel/Sheets, enabling code execution or data exfiltration against staff [verified: csv_response never sanitizes leading =/+/-/@ and tenant-controlled fields (full_name, category, findings) flow into rows opened by staff; downgraded to low since impact depends on victim's spreadsheet client formula execution/auto-open settings.]
